why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1's sample values (zero fill, default space, empty s, '*' fill) all follow from "pads s on the left with fill (a space when fill is not given) to width characters". The (s, width, fill) declaration check repeats the signature written in the expect line. Check 2 tests only the equal-length and longer cases the line names. Check 3 asks for "a heading naming that function with text under it that describes it". That is a fair reading of "a section for every function", and the function list comes from the actual exports. Check 4 is just exit code 0 with no failing tests. The stricter items (padLeft tests in the test file, the invoice example in the README) are under "Advisory (not part of any PASS/FAIL)". No PASS or FAIL condition uses mutation tests, branch or file-scope rules, or exact wording.
